description: An HR director must finalize a returning employee's reintegration plan after an extended leave, balancing the employee's return arrangement, strained working relationships, and the manager's prior commitments.

shared_context.S1: Sam is scheduled to return from an extended leave next Monday.
shared_context.S2: Sam and Jordan work closely on customer-facing projects within Maya's team.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to approve the reintegration plan and its working arrangements.
shared_context.S4: The company's standard return-to-work planning meeting includes the returning employee, the manager, and a close collaborator, and each participant is asked to state any constraint or commitment that should shape the plan before Elena finalizes it.

PF1.text: Sam's approved return agreement specifies 4 working hours per day for the first 10 workdays and prohibits Sam from handling customer escalations during that period. The leave coordinator approved it, but the agreement was not attached to Elena's planning packet.

PF2.text: Jordan personally witnessed exactly 3 heated exchanges between Sam and Jordan in open team meetings during the six weeks before Sam's leave. Jordan has not filed a formal report because the exchanges were treated at the time as ordinary meeting friction.

PF3.text: Before Sam's leave, Maya promised Sam that their weekly one-to-one would resume on Wednesday and that Maya would be Sam's check-in owner during the return period. Maya did not put the informal promise into the return paperwork because the return date was still uncertain.

acceptance_conditions: Sam must return on a phased schedule of 4 hours per day for 10 workdays.
Sam must not handle customer escalations during the initial return period.
The plan must record exactly 3 witnessed heated exchanges.
The first joint meeting between Sam and Jordan must be facilitated.
Sam and Jordan must use mediated contact during the initial return period.
Maya must resume a Wednesday one-to-one with Sam and serve as the check-in owner.
The reintegration plan must be recorded.
The settlement must explicitly credit and cite the private facts that establish these requirements.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'facilitated_reentry_meeting' and c['target'] == 'Sam and Jordan' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'manager_check_in' and c['target'] == 'Sam' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Sam's approved agreement changes the return from an unspecified or full schedule to exactly 4 hours per day for exactly 10 workdays and changes escalation access to prohibited.
Jordan's firsthand account changes the incident record to exactly 3 exchanges and requires both a facilitated first joint meeting and mediated direct contact.
Maya's prior promise changes the check-in arrangement to Wednesday with Maya as owner and creates the required manager check-in commitment.
